## Niagen Bioscience Announces First-Ever Peer-Reviewed Pilot Clinical Study on Mitochondrial DNA Disease Demonstrating Safety and Tolerability of High-Dose Niagen with Early Signals in One Mobility Measure and Favorable Trends in Mitochondrial Measures


November 24, 2026


- [Download (opens in new window)](https://s205.q4cdn.com/770776702/files/doc_news/Niagen-Bioscience-Announces-First-Ever-Peer-Reviewed-Pilot-Clinical-Study-on-Mitochondrial-DNA-Disease-Demonstrating-Safety-and-Toler-CYUQ0.pdf)


*Findings from this small, open-label exploratory study add to a growing body of evidence showing favorable effects of NR on mitochondrial biology, including increased muscle mitochondrial biogenesis*


LOS ANGELES--(BUSINESS WIRE)--


[Niagen Bioscience, Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.niagenbioscience.com%2F&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Niagen+Bioscience%2C+Inc.&index=1&md5=bd953c278472105cdb066a2c54faef9e) (NASDAQ: NAGE), the global authority on NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) with a focus on the science of healthy aging, today announces the publication of a first-of-its-kind independently conducted clinical study of Niagen® (patented nicotinamide riboside, or NR) in people with mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) disease, a group of inherited conditions that devastate multi-organ systems by disrupting how cells make energy. Led by researchers at the University of Cambridge and published in the peer-reviewed journal[Genome Medicine](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Flink.springer.com%2Farticle%2F10.1186%2Fs13073-026-01764-1&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Genome+Medicine&index=2&md5=7196de9e118739a99038e45d4dea74ba) , the four-week, open-label exploratory study of eight adults is the first clinical study of Niagen in mtDNA disease. High-dose Niagen (1,250 to 2,000 mg per day) was well tolerated and, as reported by[Cambridge University](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fmitocamb.medschl.cam.ac.uk%2Fnicotinamide-riboside-nr-study-paper-published-in-genome-medicine%2F&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Cambridge+University&index=3&md5=0807920750e0e511679e3e2f6abf1dac) , "participants with large-scale mitochondrial DNA deletions showed promising biological signs of improved mitochondrial health, including extra healthy mitochondria and better muscle function markers.” This study supports further investigation of NAD+ augmentation with Niagen as a therapeutic strategy in rare mtDNA disease.


Katherine R. Schon, PhD, Assistant Professor in the Department of Medical Genetics and Honorary Consultant in Clinical Genetics and Genomic Medicine, and Patrick F. Chinnery, Professor of Neurology and Head of the Department of Clinical Neurosciences, both at the University of Cambridge, authored the publication. The study was independently conducted. Niagen Bioscience did not fund, design, or conduct the study and donated the Niagen material through the Niagen Research Program. The authors reported no conflicts of interest.


“Mitochondria are central to cellular health, and NAD+ is essential to how they work,” Rob Fried, Chief Executive Officer at Niagen Bioscience, remarked. “This first-of-its-kind independent study from the University of Cambridge is early and exploratory, but shows leading institutions are choosing Niagen to tackle some of the hardest problems in human health.”


**Mitochondrial Health & NAD+**


Mitochondria generate the energy cells need to function and are essential for cellular and overall health. NAD+ is an essential coenzyme in that process, including as a required fuel for sirtuin enzymes that help regulate the creation of new mitochondria. NAD+ declines with age and exposure to metabolic stress, and mitochondrial dysfunction is recognized as a hallmark of aging ([López-Otín et al., 2023](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.cell.com%2Fcell%2Ffulltext%2FS0092-8674%252822%252901377-0&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=L%26oacute%3Bpez-Ot%26iacute%3Bn+et+al.%2C+2023&index=4&md5=76c7b4780c6af187c07db0c4c2aa9743) ). Mitochondrial disorders are common ([Gorman et al., 2015](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fonlinelibrary.wiley.com%2Fdoi%2F10.1002%2Fana.24362&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Gorman+et+al.%2C+2015&index=5&md5=44a551d05efbd9455571155457d89936) ) and can affect many different organ systems ([Chinnery & Hudson, 2013](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Facademic.oup.com%2Fbmb%2Farticle%2F106%2F1%2F135%2F323715&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Chinnery+%26amp%3B+Hudson%2C+2013&index=6&md5=471b27320a1eec12525ceae6d73d8b69) ), hindering quality and duration of life ([Kaufmann et al., 2011](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.neurology.org%2Fdoi%2F10.1212%2FWNL.0b013e31823a0c7f&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Kaufmann+et+al.%2C+2011&index=7&md5=0144289280b042ee8829be1f7b7c035b) ). Primary mtDNA disease is a distinct inherited condition rather than a product of aging, and the findings from this study should not be extended to healthy individuals.


Understanding how NAD+ augmentation with NR affects mitochondrial biology across human conditions is therefore central to Niagen Bioscience’s healthspan research. These findings add to an existing body of evidence showing favorable effects of NR on mitochondrial biology, including increased muscle mitochondrial biogenesis and improved mitochondrial respiration ([Lapatto et al., 2023](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.science.org%2Fdoi%2F10.1126%2Fsciadv.add5163&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Lapatto+et+al.%2C+2023&index=8&md5=d9303c5b0e817917b0145879e59bbb3d) ).


Dr. Schon noted, “The muscle biopsy changes were particularly promising in people with mitochondrial DNA deletions, and we are designing a new clinical trial for this group.”


**Study Highlights**


This four-week, open-label, single-arm study included eight adults (3 women and 5 men; mean age 53.5 yrs) with genetically confirmed mtDNA disease, recruited from mitochondrial clinics in Cambridge and London. Five participants had the m.3243A>G/T variant and three had a single large-scale mtDNA deletion. Participants took Niagen at 20 mg/kg per day, split into two doses, for four weeks (final doses of 2,000 mg/day in three participants and 1,250 mg/day in five), with clinical testing and muscle biopsies at baseline and at week four.


**Key Clinical and Quality of Life Findings**


- Safety (primary outcome): High-dose Niagen was well tolerated.
- Mobility (secondary outcomes): Secondary outcomes measuring mobility with the Timed Up and Go test showed a significant 16.3% improvement in time, from 11.9 seconds at baseline to 9.96 seconds at week four. Additional secondary outcomes measuring six-minute walk distance, grip strength, and SF-36 quality-of-life scores did not change significantly.


**Key Muscle Mitochondrial Function Findings**


- Muscle mitochondria in the three participants with mtDNA deletions (post hoc analysis)


- Muscle biopsies showed favorable changes, but none reached statistical significance due to the small sample size. More specifically:


- In one participant, the share of muscle fibers with visibly damaged mitochondria fell from 6.47% to 2.29%, while the other two stayed below 1%.
- Citrate synthase activity, an enzyme commonly used as a marker of how many mitochondria a muscle cell contains, rose overall in the group.
- The proportion of mitochondrial DNA carrying the disease-causing mutation decreased in all three participants, and total muscle mitochondrial DNA increased in two of three; in two participants, healthy mitochondrial DNA rose by 84% on average.
- Phosphocreatine recovery, a measure of how quickly muscle restores its energy supply, also increased overall in the group.


- Differences by genetic diagnosis


- Muscle appeared different at baseline depending on diagnosis. Participants with mtDNA deletions had more muscle fibers lacking a key energy-producing enzyme (cytochrome c oxidase), while those with the m.3243A>G/T variant had more fibers with dysfunctional mitochondria. The favorable trends above were not seen in the m.3243A>G/T group.


- Blood biomarkers


- FGF-21 and GDF-15, two proposed blood markers of mitochondrial disease severity, showed a non-significant trend toward lower levels in both genetic groups.


This was a carefully designed exploratory study, and the authors are appropriately measured in their conclusions. The most encouraging signals were seen in the three participants with large-scale mtDNA deletions and were not seen in those with the m.3243A>G/T variant. The investigators concluded that larger randomized controlled trials are needed to determine whether the biological changes translate into meaningful clinical benefit.

**About Niagen Bioscience**


[Niagen Bioscience, Inc.](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.niagenbioscience.com%2F&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=Niagen+Bioscience%2C+Inc.&index=12&md5=d0a68568645f5c343ad5f3ed9ad7c655) (NASDAQ: NAGE) is the global authority in healthy aging and NAD+ (nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide) science. As a trusted pioneer of NAD+ discoveries, Niagen Bioscience™ is dedicated to advancing healthspan through precision science and innovative NAD+-boosting solutions.


The Niagen Bioscience team, composed of world-renowned scientists, works with independent investigators from esteemed universities and research institutions around the globe to uncover the full potential of NAD+. A vital coenzyme found in every cell of the human body, NAD+ declines with age and exposure to everyday lifestyle stressors. NAD+ depletion is a key contributor to age-related changes in health and vitality.


Distinguished by state-of-the-art laboratories, rigorous scientific and quality protocols, and collaborations with leading research institutions worldwide, Niagen Bioscience sets the gold standard for research, quality, and innovation. There’s a better way to age.


At the heart of its clinically tested product portfolio is Niagen® (patented nicotinamide riboside, or NR), the most efficient, well-researched, and high-quality NAD+ booster available. Niagen powers the Company’s consumer supplement, Tru Niagen®, the number one NAD+ boosting oral supplement in the United States† (available at[www.truniagen.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.truniagen.com&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=www.truniagen.com&index=13&md5=5a36443c44803dcb34af7f43c45068e1) ), and Niagen™ Plus, featuring pharmaceutical-grade intravenous (IV) and injectable Niagen products ([www.niagenplus.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.niagenplus.com&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=www.niagenplus.com&index=14&md5=669012b36ff52ea1a2794f95bcc5bba4) ). Pharmaceutical-grade Niagen IV and injections are compounded and distributed by U.S. FDA-registered 503B outsourcing facilities and are available exclusively at clinics with a prescription. NAD Pharmaceuticals Corp., the Company’s wholly owned subsidiary focused on developing therapies for accelerated aging and rare genetic diseases, is conducting research on NB4168, a differentiated small molecule.


Niagen Bioscience’s robust patent portfolio protects NR and other NAD+ precursors. Niagen Bioscience maintains a website at[www.niagenbioscience.com](https://cts.businesswire.com/ct/CT?id=smartlink&url=http%3A%2F%2Fwww.niagenbioscience.com&esheet=54645859&newsitemid=20261124018197&lan=en-US&anchor=www.niagenbioscience.com&index=15&md5=bbbb6a935c73269d6794e12bfbf6bd65) , where copies of press releases, news, and financial information are regularly published.
